## This game

A new game. You play Black, so you move first.

Rules: Chinese area scoring, with 7 points of komi for White; a level score is a draw. Simple ko: an immediate recapture is refused, and the board marks the ko point when there is one. Suicide is not allowed. An invalid move is refused with the rule it broke, and the turn stays with you. The game ends after two passes in a row or a resignation; a game that reaches 243 moves is scored where it stands. After two passes the engine scores the position as it stands and decides itself which stones are dead.

## Opponents

Your opponent is KataGo playing in the style of a human of the rank you choose. The ladder, weakest to strongest: 20k, 18k, 16k, 14k, 12k, 10k, 8k, 6k, 4k, 2k, 1d, 3d, 5d, 7d, 9d. You choose the rank with `choose_opponent(rank)` before the first move; it holds for the whole game, and you choose again in the next game.

## Tools

- Go: `choose_opponent(rank)`, `board()`, `play(move)` with a point or `pass`, and `resign()`.
- Files: `read_file(path)` and `list_files(path)` to read, and `apply_patch` to create, change and delete any file in your working directory.

You may write and run code. Use it only to inspect the current position and keep records — for example, to count stones or liberties, or check whether a move is legal. Do not build or use a Go engine, run Monte Carlo, search over sequences of future moves, or write a program that chooses, ranks or recommends moves.

## How this session ends

Play until the game is over. The final result comes back from your last Go call, followed by a closing note. Before you end the session after a game, write down in your working directory whatever will help the next session play better. The session ends when you end your turn.
I’ll stay at 20k for game 39, read the latest reviews, and record every response. As Black, I’ll aim for a broad base and check both area and eye space before committing to defense.

const cols="ABCDEFGHJ";
function parseBoard(r){const s=r.content.filter(x=>x.type==="text").map(x=>x.text).join("
");const b={};for(const line of s.split("
")){const m=line.match(/^\s*([1-9])\s+([.XO](?:\s+[.XO]){8})\s+[1-9]\s*$/);if(m)m[2].split(/\s+/).forEach((v,i)=>b[cols[i]+m[1]]=v);}return {s,b};}
function neighbors(p){const x=cols.indexOf(p[0]),y=Number(p[1]);return [[x-1,y],[x+1,y],[x,y-1],[x,y+1]].filter(([a,z])=>a>=0&&a<9&&z>=1&&z<=9).map(([a,z])=>cols[a]+z);}
function inspect(b){const seen=new Set(),groups=[],regions=[];for(const p of Object.keys(b)){if(seen.has(p))continue;const c=b[p],stack=[p],stones=[],lib=new Set(),border=new Set();seen.add(p);while(stack.length){const q=stack.pop();stones.push(q);for(const n of neighbors(q)){if(b[n]===c&&!seen.has(n)){seen.add(n);stack.push(n);}else if(b[n]!==c){if(b[n]===".")lib.add(n);else border.add(b[n]);}}}if(c===".")regions.push({points:stones.sort(),border:[...border]});else groups.push({color:c,stones:stones.sort(),liberties:[...lib].sort()});}return {groups,regions};}

3. Check two eyes for every major group before treating it as safe. Connected stones and many present liberties are not proof of life. Preserve eye space and a base before filling internal points.
4. In capture reading, rebuild the position after each capture. Captured stones open liberties for adjacent enemy groups. The D8/E9 sacrifice in game 1 overlooked this.

# Game 39: Black vs 20k — W+20

Played 2026-10-06. 9×9, Chinese area scoring, komi 7, simple ko.
Consecutive passes at moves 81–82 ended the game.
Official W+20 matches Black34 versus White47+7.
Final captures: Black9, White13. Final stones: Black27, White31.
Every final displayed stone survived; no dead-stone removal or neutral area.
20k record: eight wins, twenty-five losses, two draws. Retain20k.

## Records and verification

game-039.sgf preserves all82 actual moves, including both passes.
game-039-log.json preserves selection, all42 play attempts saved before continuing, current-board inventories, manual notes, exact actual moves, capture events, row counts and replay evidence.
One A2 attempt between moves72 and73 was refused as suicide; it changed neither board nor turn and is excluded from SGF.
Actual-history replay matched all42 returned full boards and every capture count, including selection and final score. The refused response had no board.
The final displayed move number83 denotes the next turn.
game-039-inspection.js preserves the current-position inspection/recording helper.
Code recorded and inspected current positions, replayed actual history, counted final area and converted actual moves to SGF. All choices and hypothetical lines were manual. No engine, Monte Carlo, future-sequence search or automated move recommendation.

## Exact moves

1 B C3, 2 W E5, 3 B G7, 4 W C5, 5 B C7, 6 W D7, 7 B C8, 8 W D8, 9 B E3, 10 W F4, 11 B D3, 12 W F3, 13 B G5, 14 W G3, 15 B G4, 16 W F2, 17 B E2, 18 W D6, 19 B G6, 20 W B4, 21 B B3, 22 W B6, 23 B B7, 24 W F8, 25 B G8, 26 W F7, 27 B D4, 28 W G9, 29 B H8, 30 W H4, 31 B H5, 32 W H3, 33 B H9, 34 W J7, 35 B J8, 36 W J5, 37 B J6, 38 W H6, 39 B H7, 40 W F5, 41 B J6, 42 W J4, 43 B F9, 44 W E9, 45 B G9, 46 W E7, 47 B C6, 48 W B5, 49 B D5, 50 W A3, 51 B C4, 52 W A4, 53 B A2, 54 W A7, 55 B A8, 56 W B2, 57 B C2, 58 W A1, 59 B B1, 60 W C1, 61 B D1, 62 W F1, 63 B B1, 64 W C9, 65 B B8, 66 W B9, 67 B A6, 68 W C1, 69 B A5, 70 W A7, 71 B A6, 72 W D9, 73 B B1, 74 W A9, 75 B A2, 76 W A7, 77 B E1, 78 W A5, 79 B E4, 80 W F6, 81 B pass, 82 W pass.

## Three bases again, without sufficient room or life turns

C3/G7/C7 claimed three bases against White E5/C5/D7.
C8 met D8. E3 and D3 broadened and joined the lower group; E2 retained its lower-right boundary.
G5/G4/G6 broadened and joined the right before contact.
These connections worked against played replies, but did not prove life or a winning opening.

At move10 the manual selected outline was upper-left A/B/C rows6–9=12, lower A–E rows1–3=15, right G/H/J rows4–9=18: conditional45.
This was a target, not territory, and had no reduction margin.
Upper B6/A6, lower A3, and right G9/H4/J4/J5 were contested or subsequently lost.
G9 was eventually restored by capture and F9 added, but the lower/right surviving regions remained too small.

D4/D5/C4 were actual expansion: three added connected central points.
E1/E4 added two late boundary points.
They improved the final lower region to18, but could not replace a lost upper region.
No earlier move is established as an optimal or winning replacement.
The upper group had one connected top room and no completed two-eye proof throughout. C6 at47 reduced its liberties while trying to attack the adjacent left chain.
The attempt to kill that chain had three boundary fronts: A2 below, A5/A6 left, and A8/B8/C9 above, plus the B1/C1 ko.
Treating these as separately affordable turns failed.

An early outline is useful only if it includes concrete boundary and division turns against intervening replies.
Do not infer that three corner footholds sum to45 secure area.
Earlier C9 protection or a different two-base plan needs fresh reading, not an assumed winning substitution.

## Right invasion: a capture-rebuild error, then correct shared eyes

H8 connected before H9. H9 at33 ataried G9 atF9.
White J7/J5 tried a bridge inside the right room.
Black J8 created trueJ9, then J6 at37 cut the bridge but was isolated with soleH6.
I predicted W H6, B H7 would immediately capture H6/J7.
That prediction was WRONG: White H6 at38 first captured J6, reopening J6 for both White stones.
Current inventory corrected this before H7.

Black H7 at39 ataried H6 and J7 atJ6.
The corrected limited lines were W J6, B J4 capturing H6/J6/J7/J5 (soleJ4 after their join), or W J4, B J6 capturing H6/J7.
Actual White F5 ignored both ataris; J6 at41 captured H6/J7, and White J4 saved J5.

Final true shared eyes:
- H6: G6/H5/H7/J6.
- J7: H7/J6/J8.
- J9: H9/J8.

Isolated J6 has H6/J7; the main has allthree.
Every boundary group retains another eye on an enemy fill, so either shared-eye entry is suicide.
Do not fill H6/J7 just to join J6.
The physical capture followed ignored ataris; the review establishes only the specified local alternatives, not exhaustive forced capture.

F9 at43 captured G9 after its atari was ignored.
F9 was isolated with E9/G9; White E9 left soleG9.
G9 at45 was necessary to connect it. An ataried isolated boundary does not support a true shared-eye claim.
Final right12 main stones + isolatedJ6 + three eyes =16.

## Bottom cut, ko, and one refused suicide

A2 at53 tried to contain the six-stone left chain but was isolated.
White B2, Black C2, White A1 captured A2 at58.
This differed from the earlier manual line that assumed White B1 first.

At that point White A1 and B2 each had BOTH A2 and B1.
They were separate groups. Filling A2 did not capture either while B1 remained empty.
Black B1 at59 was itself isolated with soleC1; White C1 captured it.
D1 at61 capped C1, and B1 at63 captured C1 after White F1 ignored its atari.
That one-stone capture with soleC1 implies a transient C1 ko; the returned board after White C9 showed no current ko.
White C1 at68 legally recaptured B1 and the tool explicitly marked B1 as ko.
Black played A5 rather than immediate recapture.
Black B1 at73 later legally captured C1 again.

A2 attempted after White D9 at72 was refused as suicide.
I had again incorrectly assumed it captured A1/B2; both still had B1.
No board change or White reply followed the refusal.
Black B1 at73 first removed that liberty. Then A2 at75 legally captured A1/B2.
This is a concrete reason to inspect proposed-move legality and ALL liberties before relying on a capture, especially in a ko fight.
The code did not select moves; a current-position legality check is allowed and would have prevented this attempt.

## The left attack failed because our own captures were reversed

White C9 at64 ataried the upper four stones atB8.
B8 joined A8 but White B9 at66 left six upper stones onlyA9.
A6 at67 captured White A7 and reopened A7 for the upper group.
It supplied an outside liberty, not two eyes.
The upper then had A7/A9; isolated A6 had A5/A7, and the left White chain had A2/A5.

Black A5 at69 joined A6 and ataried the left chain atA2, but the A5/A6 pair itself had onlyA7.
White A7 at70 captured that pair, reopening A5/A6 for the left White chain while atariing the upper atA9.
The proposed threat did not stay an atari after this capture.
Black A6 at71 captured A7 again and reopened A7, but White D9 joined its top stones to the main group.

Black B1 at73 addressed the ko, allowing White A9 at74.
Final local upper reading then:
- Six upper stones had onlyA7.
- A6 had A5/A7.
- Left six White stones had A2/A5.
- B A7 would join eight Black stones but leave them onlyA5; W A5 captures all eight while retainingA2.
- B A5 instead joins A6 with onlyA7; W A7 captures A5/A6 and the six upper stones, reopening liberties for the left chain.
- B A2 captures A1/B2 but does not save the upper; W A7 captures the six upper stones and reopens B7/C6 for the left chain.
These are limited local lines; no external capture rescue was verified.

Actual A2 at75 secured the lower eyes, White A7 at76 captured A8/B7/B8/C6/C7/C8.
A6 then had soleA5. B A5 was suicide because the left White chain retained B7/C6.
White A5 at78 captured A6 after Black E1.
Thus six upper stones were physically lost, along with two played incarnations of A6 and the A5 sacrificed at69.
Do not call a captured intruder's opening an eye or a rescue without reading the immediate recapture and ALL reopened liberties.

## Surviving lower life and final score

E1 at77 joined D1 to E2; E4 at79 added the last lower boundary point.
White F6 at80 took the other contested point and joined its upper/lower groups.
All remaining empty regions were single-color bordered.

Lower main12 stones, isolatedA2 and isolatedB1 share four true eyes:
- A1: A2/B1.
- B2: A2/B1/B3/C2.
- C1: B1/C2/D1.
- D2: C2/D1/D3/E2.

Main retains B2/C1/D2; A2 retains A1/B2; B1 retains A1/B2/C1.
Every boundary group retains another eye on either attempted enemy fill.
No connection by filling an eye was needed.
Lower14 stones+4 eyes=18; right13 stones+3 eyes=16.
Black27+7=34. White31+16=47.
White empty points: A6; A8/B7/B8/C6/C7/C8; E6/E8; G1/G2/H1/H2/J1/J2/J3.
Rows1–9 Black=5,5,4,4,3,3,3,3,4; White=4,4,5,5,6,6,6,6,5.
No dead or neutral points. 47+7−34=20 matches official W+20.

## Carry forward

1. Retain20k: eight wins, twenty-five losses, two draws.
2. Broad bases need room AND enough boundary/life turns. Conditional45 with three unfinished bases had no reduction margin.
3. Read complete capture/reply changes. W H6 captured J6 and reopened J6; W A7 captured A5/A6 and restored the left chain's liberties.
4. Before a proposed capture, list every enemy group's current liberties and check legality. A1/B2 each retained B1; A2 was suicide until B1 became Black.
5. A6's capture of A7 reopened a liberty but did not establish life. A5 was an ataried sacrifice, not a durable ko threat.
6. Keep the correct H6/J7/J9 and A1/B2/C1/D2 same-color shared-eye proofs. Do not connect by unnecessarily filling eyes.
7. Outcome does not establish move values or an earlier winning alternative. Preserve the distinction between limited local lines and exhaustive death claims.
8. Replay matched42 full boards/captures, SGF saved82 actual moves, and one refused suicide is separately recorded.

    "Manual: joined cap against H4, retaining upper-right room; H4 removes second selected point.",
    "Manual: now joined through H8; close top endpoint and atari G9 at F9. Conditional upper-left11 + lower16 + right16 =43; reductions elsewhere still pending.",
    "Manual: contain J7 upward and create true J9 (H9/J8 boundaries). Limited direct invasion lines: W H7 B H6 W J6 B J5 captures three; W J6 B J5 W H7 B H6 captures three. Other defenses require fresh reading.",
    "Manual: cut bridge J5-J7. J6 has H6; W H7 leaves H6 sole liberty for H7/J7, B H6 captures two. W J4 saves J5 but B H7 captures J7 and makes same-color shared H6/J7 plus main J9. W H6 B H7 captures H6 and J7. Limited local lines, no exhaustive search.",
    "Correction: W H6 captured isolated J6, reopening J6; prior prediction of immediate two-stone capture was wrong. H7 now ataries H6 and J7 at J6. W J6 connects H6/J7/J5 but leaves only J4, B J4 captures four; W J4 saves J5, B J6 captures H6/J7.",
    "Manual: capture H6 and J7 after ignored ataris. Isolated J6 shares true H6 (G6/H5/H7/J6) and J7(H7/J6/J8) with main; each retains other eye. Main also true J9.",
    "Manual: capture ataried G9, restore G9 and add F9 outside original right outline. Isolated F9 has E9/G9; if W E9, B G9 connects rather than pretending G9 remains a true shared eye with an ataried boundary.",
    "Manual: connect ataried F9 to main; necessary since F9 only G9. Right guaranteed core: twelve main stones plus isolated J6 and true H6/J7/J9 =16, F6 unsettled.",
    "Manual: extend upper group downward and pressure B6/C5; upper room is still one connected region, no two-eye proof. Need expansion or capture/connection, not cosmetic top filling.",

    "Manual: cap A7 and contain left groups in one adjacent A5/A6 room. W A6 joins both then B A5 captures eight; W A5 B A6 captures eight. A8 isolated A9/B8; W B8 has only B9, so B B9 captures that cutter and reopens B8.",

## Lessons to use immediately
1. Count prospective area early, especially after about 10-16 moves. With all 81 points assigned, Black needs at least 45 for a win with 7 komi; 44-37 is a draw. If there is neutral area, compare actual totals instead.
2. Center influence must yield territory, an attack, or access to a viable invasion. Game 1 built a narrow central chain while White took both sides.
3. Check two eyes for every major group before treating it as safe. Connected stones and many present liberties are not proof of life. Preserve eye space and a base before filling internal points.
4. In capture reading, rebuild the position after each capture. Captured stones open liberties for adjacent enemy groups. The D8/E9 sacrifice in game 1 overlooked this.
5. Ko eyes are not unconditional eyes. Game 1's lower D2 and upper E8 spaces depended on vulnerable isolated Black stones. Owning two such ko positions does not by itself guarantee double-ko life.
6. Do not repeat the complete opening E5 C5 E3 D7 F7 G5 G6 H6 G7 G3 without reconsidering its territorial consequences. E5 itself was not shown to be wrong.
